summary.text: 分 now commonly means “divide” or “part.” Early forms are analyzed as a knife between marks representing separated things; one paleographic analysis also assigns 八 a sound role, though the sound evidence is not a close match.

formation.text: A composite formation traditionally analyzed as semantic: 刀 depicts the knife and 八 represents the things separated around it. A modern paleographic analysis also proposes that 八 supplied a phonetic cue. The curated Shang oracle-script image shows this arrangement, but the image and surviving evidence do not establish the makers’ intended functions on their own.

components.text: The visible form is 八. In this character it is interpreted pictorially as two separated things. A paleographic analysis additionally treats it as phonetic; the component readings provide a possible but imperfect comparison, not proof of that role.

sound_limitation.text: The cited paleographic account proposes a phonetic role, but the available sound comparison is not close in the cited reconstructions and does not establish the role or its precise historical mechanism.

sound.text: The proposed comparison is between 八 and 分 in the divide reading. Mandarin bā and fēn differ; in the cited Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese reconstructions, 八 is *pˤret and 分 is *pə[n], also not a close rhyme match.

components.text: 刀 depicts the knife in the proposed separation scene and is the semantic component in the traditional analysis. The cited accounts do not identify a separate earlier form for this component here.

history.text: The selected Shang oracle-script redrawing places marks on either side of 刀. Oracle-bone and bronze forms are reported to contain 八 and 刀, and a form inventory also records Chu manuscript and Small Seal forms. The available material does not establish a complete sequence of graphic changes between them.

The Shuowen Jiezi glosses 分 as “separate/distinguish” and explains it through 八 and 刀, with the knife separating things. This is an early dictionary interpretation, not independent proof of the original graphic motivation.

uncertainties.text: Analysis of 八 is disputed: one account treats it as pictorial and phonetic, while another labels it iconic. Reconstructions show a possible sound relationship but not a close match; they do not establish the component’s proposed phonetic role.

A reported oracle-bone place-name use does not establish the ordinary earliest lexical meaning, and its proposed identification with the Linfen area is unverified here. The earliest secure ordinary sense and the links among separation, allocation, distinction, and quantitative units remain unresolved by this dossier.

senses.text: The traditional Shuowen gloss is “separate/distinguish.” The dossier does not establish that this is the earliest ordinary lexical sense; an oracle-bone place-name use is reported but does not settle that question.

senses.gloss: allocate fields and settlements; allotted duty or status
senses.period: early textual and inscriptional uses; individual dates unresolved
senses.text: An inscription is cited for allocating fields and settlements, and Warring States manuscript uses are reported for role or status. A separate phonological entry gives a reading for “allotted duty,” but the relationship of that use to the divide reading is not demonstrated.
The Shang Yang measure inscription securely attests 分 in a fractional measurement expression by 344 BCE. This dates that use, not its origin or its precedence over the separation sense.
Part, share, and segment are current glosses in the supplied dictionary data. The dossier does not independently establish their chronology or a specific path of development from separation.
The character is used for a time unit. Japanese examples attest this use in 1798–1802, but do not determine when the Chinese sense arose.

developments.text: Allocation is plausibly related to separating or distributing things, but the dossier does not document the semantic transition directly.
A fractional unit is plausibly related to dividing quantities, but the cited dated inscription establishes the use rather than the development from the separation sense.
“Part” can be understood as the result of separation, but the dossier supplies current glosses rather than a dated record of this semantic development.
The dossier records time-unit uses but does not establish whether they developed from fractional measurement or through another route.

limitations.text: The reported oracle-bone place-name use and proposed geographic identification do not establish an ordinary earliest lexical sense. No complete, dated semantic sequence is available here.
The supplied Japanese attestations establish Japanese uses only; they do not establish the chronology of the Chinese character or word.

overview.text: 分 commonly means “divide” or “part.” Its traditional analysis pictures a knife separating two things; one paleographic account also proposes 八 as a sound cue, though that comparison is imperfect.

components.text: 八 is read as two separated things in this character; one analysis also proposes a sound role, but the historical comparison is imperfect.
刀 depicts the knife that separates the things in the traditional explanation.

takeaway.text: The dossier does not establish which ordinary lexical sense came first or a complete path from “separate” to the unit senses.

relationships.text: 八 is interpreted as pictorially representing the separated things in 分.
One paleographic analysis assigns 八 a phonetic role, but the cited sound comparisons are imperfect and do not independently establish that role.
刀 depicts the knife in the proposed scene of separation.
The traditional analysis assigns 刀 the role of separating things, contributing to the character’s sense.
